changeSet.comment: nexus_test.add_fk_not_valid(regclass, text, text, regclass, text, text): plpgsql wrapper for ALTER TABLE .. ADD CONSTRAINT .. FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, p_column) REFERENCES .. (tenant_id, p_ref_column) p_extra NOT VALID -- a Postgres-only ALTER TABLE extension with no jOOQ typed-DSL form (batch 10 review fold-in). p_table/p_ref are regclass so PostgreSQL resolves each table identity with no string to validate; p_name/p_column/p_ref_column are %I-quoted identifiers; p_extra is the caller-supplied ON UPDATE/ON DELETE clause fragment (e.g. 'ON DELETE RESTRICT'), inserted via %s since it is not a single identifier -- always a fixed literal from Java call sites, never end-user input. Every caller's composite FK is (tenant_id, X) -> (tenant_id, Y), so tenant_id is hardcoded as the first column on both sides rather than adding two more parameters no call site would vary. SECURITY INVOKER so the caller's own (superuser, in every test) privilege authorizes the ALTER TABLE.

changeSet.author: nexus-cbo4a
changeSet.comment: nexus_test.grant_execute_on_function(text, text): plpgsql wrapper for GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION p_signature TO p_role (nexus-cbo4a batch 11). GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION has no jOOQ typed-DSL form -- jOOQ's GRANT DSL (DSLContext#grant/ GrantOnStep#on) targets tables (Table<?>/Name/String identifiers), not a function's parenthesized argument-type signature, which is what Postgres's GRANT ... ON FUNCTION syntax actually requires after the function name. p_signature is the caller-supplied function-name-plus-arg-types fragment (e.g. "nexus.gc_quarantine_orphans(int, text, text, text, text, int)"), inserted via %s since it is not a single identifier -- always a fixed literal from Java call sites, never end-user input, exactly the same shape add_fk_not_valid_composite3's p_extra clause already uses; p_role is %I-quoted. SECURITY INVOKER so the caller's own (superuser, in every test) privilege authorizes the GRANT. This pattern recurs raw across ~15 other test files today (out of nexus-cbo4a batch 11's scope) -- a follow-up batch can rewire them onto this same function.
changeSet.rollback: DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS nexus_test.grant_execute_on_function(text, text)

changeSet.author: nexus-ft04v.4
changeSet.comment: nexus_test.insert_chunk_bare_vector(text, text, bytea, int): plpgsql wrapper inserting one nexus.chunks row with a BARE (unqualified) ::vector cast built entirely server-side -- for tests that seed vector data at a migration point BEFORE search-path-001-relocate-vector-extensions.xml has relocated the pgvector extension into the nexus schema (Hygiene002CollectionAttributesWalkTest.walkPopulatesEveryBranchAcrossTwoTenants...: hygiene-002-1 runs before search-path-001 in the changelog, so a jOOQ-generated INSERT -- whose compiled binding casts to the schema-qualified "nexus.vector" fixed at codegen time against a FULLY relocated cluster -- fails with "type nexus.vector does not exist" at that point; a bare, unqualified ::vector cast resolves via whatever the connecting role's search_path finds at EXECUTION time, exactly like Hygiene001NotNullMigrationRlsTest's own seedLegacyChunkAndManifest raw-SQL precedent, generalised into a reusable function so no Java caller needs its own raw SQL string). The bare cast is deliberately the ONLY form valid against BOTH substrates this function's callers use: a pre-walk dedicated container (extension still in public, in every role's default search_path) and the shared, fully-migrated cluster (extension relocated to nexus, which search-path-002 adds to the migrating role's own search_path) -- a schema-qualified cast picks one and breaks the other. p_dim selects which embedding_<dim> column receives the value via %I-quoted dynamic column name; the "[0.1,0.1,...]" literal of length p_dim is built via generate_series/string_agg, never string-concatenated in Java. SECURITY INVOKER so the caller's own privilege authorizes the INSERT.
changeSet.rollback: DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS nexus_test.insert_chunk_bare_vector(text, text, bytea, int)

changeSet.author: nexus-3wh8d.13
changeSet.comment: RDR-225: nexus_test.insert_chunk_bare_vector supplies embedding_model once nexus.chunks has the column (vectors-030-1). The function is shared by two kinds of caller: the pre-walk dedicated containers (Hygiene002CollectionAttributesWalkTest, Hygiene004OwnerGrammarUnderscoreTest), where the column does not exist yet and the original three-column-key INSERT is the only valid one, and any caller on a fully walked cluster, where the row must carry its collection's model (a NOT NULL partition key, and the model partition's dimension CHECK). The function therefore asks information_schema which shape it is running against, at execution time, and takes the model from the collection's catalog_collections row; a collection with no row is refused by name instead of by the composite foreign key. Same signature, so the generated Routines.insertChunkBareVector is unchanged. SECURITY INVOKER.

changeSet.comment: nexus_test.p225_ts3_delete_and_reinsert(text, text, bytea): RDR-225 TS3 case (b) against the partitioned nexus.chunks (nexus-3wh8d.8). changeSet.author: nexus-cbo4a
changeSet.comment: nexus_test.lateral_cross_rows_1024(text, text): the row count of the bare CROSS JOIN LATERAL nearest-foreign-centroid shape over p_collection's 1024-dim chunks, with no hnsw.* or access-path settings of its own, so it runs under whatever the caller's session set (TaxonomyAssignCrossLateralHnswTest's no-row-hazard reproduction). The ORDER BY needs OPERATOR(nexus.<=>) for the HNSW index to serve it, which the jOOQ DSL has no operator for. EXECUTE with literal values plans the statement once with the values in hand, as the single pgjdbc execution it replaces did. SECURITY INVOKER.
changeSet.sql: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION nexus_test.lateral_cross_rows_1024(p_tenant text, p_collection text) RETURNS bigint LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY INVOKER AS $$ DECLARE v_n bigint; BEGIN EXECUTE format( 'SELECT count(*) FROM (' ' SELECT c.chash AS h, c.embedding_1024 AS e FROM nexus.chunks c' ' WHERE c.tenant_id = %L AND c.collection = %L AND c.embedding_1024 IS NOT NULL' ') b CROSS JOIN LATERAL (' ' SELECT ct.topic_id t FROM nexus.taxonomy_centroids ct' ' WHERE ct.collection <> %L AND ct.embedding_1024 IS NOT NULL' ' ORDER BY ct.embedding_1024 OPERATOR(nexus.<=>) b.e, ct.topic_id LIMIT 1' ') n', p_tenant, p_collection, p_collection) INTO v_n; RETURN v_n; END; $$;
changeSet.rollback: DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS nexus_test.lateral_cross_rows_1024(text, text)

changeSet.author: nexus-cbo4a
changeSet.comment: nexus_test.lock_table(text, text): plpgsql wrapper for LOCK TABLE (nexus-cbo4a batch 6) for PgContainerHelper#lockTable. jOOQ has no LOCK clause. p_table is text cast to regclass inside the body, so PostgreSQL resolves the identity and there is no string to validate; p_mode is checked (non-NULL, one of the eight PostgreSQL lock modes) before it reaches format(). The lock is taken inside the caller's transaction and lives until it ends, which is the point: a caller holds it open on a connection of its own. Returns true so the call is an ordinary one-column select. SECURITY INVOKER so the caller's own privilege authorizes the LOCK.
changeSet.rollback: DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS nexus_test.lock_table(text, text)

changeSet.author: nexus-cbo4a
changeSet.comment: nexus_test.catalog_snapshot(): one text row per catalog entry, prefixed with its section (nexus-cbo4a batch 8), for PristineCloneSkipTest, which diffs a clone's catalog before and after applyProductSchema. The nineteen catalog reads (relations with owner, ACL, reloptions and RLS flags, column ACLs, functions with a body hash, schemas, default ACLs, policies, constraints, indexes, triggers, event triggers, extensions, sequences, views, materialized views, the database ACL and settings, roles, memberships, and the changelog journal minus the columns a rerun rewrites) have no typed jOOQ form: pg_get_indexdef, pg_get_constraintdef and format() over several catalogs. They moved here verbatim from that test's Java strings. System schemas are excluded. STABLE and SECURITY INVOKER; it reads catalogs only and lists itself in the function section like any other nexus_test function, so a before and after snapshot still compare equal.
changeSet.sql: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION nexus_test.catalog_snapshot() RETURNS SETOF text LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY INVOKER AS $$ SELECT 'relation: ' || t FROM ( SELECT format('%s.%s kind=%s owner=%s acl=%s opts=%s rls=%s/%s persist=%s part=%s', n.nspname, c.relname, c.relkind, pg_get_userbyid(c.relowner), c.relacl, c.reloptions, c.relrowsecurity, c.relforcerowsecurity, c.relpersistence, c.relispartition) FROM pg_class c JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace WHERE n.nspname NOT IN ('pg_catalog','information_schema') AND n.nspname NOT LIKE 'pg_toast%' AND n.nspname NOT LIKE 'pg_temp%' ) s(t) UNION ALL SELECT 'columnacl: ' || t FROM ( SELECT format('%s.%s.%s %s', n.nspname, c.relname, a.attname, a.attacl) FROM pg_attribute a JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = a.attrelid JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace WHERE a.attacl IS NOT NULL AND n.nspname NOT IN ('pg_catalog','information_schema') AND n.nspname NOT LIKE 'pg_toast%' AND n.nspname NOT LIKE 'pg_temp%' ) s(t) UNION ALL SELECT 'function: ' || t FROM ( SELECT format('%s.%s(%s) owner=%s acl=%s cfg=%s secdef=%s vol=%s kind=%s body=%s', n.nspname, p.proname, pg_get_function_identity_arguments(p.oid), pg_get_userbyid(p.proowner), p.proacl, p.proconfig, p.prosecdef, p.provolatile, p.prokind, md5(p.prosrc)) FROM pg_proc p JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = p.pronamespace WHERE n.nspname NOT IN ('pg_catalog','information_schema') AND n.nspname NOT LIKE 'pg_toast%' AND n.nspname NOT LIKE 'pg_temp%' ) s(t) UNION ALL SELECT 'schema: ' || t FROM ( SELECT format('%s owner=%s acl=%s', n.nspname, pg_get_userbyid(n.nspowner), n.nspacl) FROM pg_namespace n WHERE n.nspname NOT LIKE 'pg_toast%' AND n.nspname NOT LIKE 'pg_temp%' ) s(t) UNION ALL SELECT 'defaultacl: ' || t FROM ( SELECT format('role=%s ns=%s type=%s acl=%s', pg_get_userbyid(defaclrole), coalesce(defaclnamespace::regnamespace::text, '-'), defaclobjtype, defaclacl) FROM pg_default_acl ) s(t) UNION ALL SELECT 'policy: ' || t FROM ( SELECT format('%s on %s cmd=%s permissive=%s roles=%s using=%s check=%s', polname, polrelid::regclass, polcmd, polpermissive, (SELECT string_agg(CASE WHEN r = 0 THEN 'public' ELSE pg_get_userbyid(r) END, ',' ORDER BY r) FROM unnest(polroles) r), pg_get_expr(polqual, polrelid), pg_get_expr(polwithcheck, polrelid)) FROM pg_policy ) s(t) UNION ALL SELECT 'constraint: ' || t FROM ( SELECT format('%s on %s %s validated=%s', conname, conrelid::regclass, pg_get_constraintdef(oid), convalidated) FROM pg_constraint WHERE connamespace NOT IN ('pg_catalog'::regnamespace, 'information_schema'::regnamespace) ) s(t) UNION ALL SELECT 'index: ' || t FROM ( SELECT format('%s valid=%s ready=%s', pg_get_indexdef(i.indexrelid), i.indisvalid, i.indisready) FROM pg_index i JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = i.indexrelid JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace WHERE n.nspname NOT IN ('pg_catalog','information_schema') AND n.nspname NOT LIKE 'pg_toast%' AND n.nspname NOT LIKE 'pg_temp%' ) s(t) UNION ALL SELECT 'trigger: ' || t FROM ( SELECT format('%s on %s %s enabled=%s', tgname, tgrelid::regclass, pg_get_triggerdef(oid), tgenabled) FROM pg_trigger WHERE NOT tgisinternal ) s(t) UNION ALL SELECT 'eventtrigger: ' || t FROM ( SELECT format('%s event=%s owner=%s enabled=%s fn=%s tags=%s', evtname, evtevent, pg_get_userbyid(evtowner), evtenabled, evtfoid::regproc, evttags) FROM pg_event_trigger ) s(t) UNION ALL SELECT 'extension: ' || t FROM ( SELECT format('%s %s ns=%s', extname, extversion, extnamespace::regnamespace) FROM pg_extension ) s(t) UNION ALL SELECT 'sequence: ' || t FROM ( SELECT format('%s.%s owner=%s type=%s start=%s inc=%s max=%s min=%s cache=%s cycle=%s last=%s', schemaname, sequencename, sequenceowner, data_type, start_value, increment_by, max_value, min_value, cache_size, cycle, last_value) FROM pg_sequences ) s(t) UNION ALL SELECT 'view: ' || t FROM ( SELECT format('%s.%s owner=%s def=%s', schemaname, viewname, viewowner, md5(definition)) FROM pg_views WHERE schemaname NOT IN ('pg_catalog','information_schema') ) s(t) UNION ALL SELECT 'matview: ' || t FROM ( SELECT format('%s.%s owner=%s def=%s', schemaname, matviewname, matviewowner, md5(definition)) FROM pg_matviews ) s(t) UNION ALL SELECT 'database: ' || t FROM ( SELECT format('owner=%s acl=%s connlimit=%s', pg_get_userbyid(datdba), datacl, datconnlimit) FROM pg_database WHERE datname = current_database() ) s(t) UNION ALL SELECT 'databasesetting: ' || t FROM ( SELECT format('role=%s cfg=%s', CASE WHEN setrole = 0 THEN '-' ELSE pg_get_userbyid(setrole) END, setconfig) FROM pg_db_role_setting WHERE setdatabase = (SELECT oid FROM pg_database WHERE datname = current_database()) ) s(t) UNION ALL SELECT 'role: ' || t FROM ( SELECT format('%s super=%s inherit=%s createrole=%s createdb=%s login=%s repl=%s bypassrls=%s conn=%s cfg=%s', rolname, rolsuper, rolinherit, rolcreaterole, rolcreatedb, rolcanlogin, rolreplication, rolbypassrls, rolconnlimit, rolconfig) FROM pg_roles ) s(t) UNION ALL SELECT 'membership: ' || t FROM ( SELECT format('%s in %s admin=%s', pg_get_userbyid(member), pg_get_userbyid(roleid), admin_option) FROM pg_auth_members ) s(t) UNION ALL SELECT 'journal: ' || t FROM ( SELECT format('%s|%s|%s|%s', id, author, filename, md5sum) FROM public.databasechangelog ) s(t); $$;
changeSet.rollback: DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS nexus_test.catalog_snapshot()

changeSet.author: nexus-cbo4a
changeSet.comment: nexus_test.explain_plan(text, boolean, boolean, boolean, boolean): one text row per line of EXPLAIN (ANALYZE a, VERBOSE v, BUFFERS b, COSTS c) p_stmt (nexus-cbo4a batch C), for PgContainerHelper#explainPlanWith. jOOQ's DSLContext#explain runs a plain EXPLAIN only: no ANALYZE (so no actual loops= counts), no VERBOSE, no BUFFERS and no COSTS OFF, which several plan-shape tests read. The option list is built here from the four booleans, so no caller supplies option text; the statement text is the only string, and the Java wrapper accepts a jOOQ Query only, rendered with every bind inlined (EXPLAIN takes no bind parameters through EXECUTE). A plpgsql FOR .. IN EXECUTE returns every plan row, with no row cap. SECURITY INVOKER and no SET clause: it runs inside the caller's transaction, as the caller's role, so the caller's SET LOCAL planner pins and tenant GUC apply to the plan, and ANALYZE executes the statement under the caller's own row-level security.
changeSet.rollback: DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS nexus_test.explain_plan(text, boolean, boolean, boolean, boolean)

changeSet.author: nexus-cbo4a
changeSet.comment: nexus_test.cosine_order(nexus.vector, nexus.vector): the pgvector cosine-distance operator (nexus.<=>) as a function, so a typed jOOQ ORDER BY can carry it (nexus-cbo4a batch D). jOOQ has no form for OPERATOR(nexus.<=>), and Routines.cosineDistance1 is pgvector's C function, which an HNSW index never serves. This one is meant to be served: LANGUAGE sql with a single-expression body, IMMUTABLE, PARALLEL SAFE, not STRICT, no SET clause and SECURITY INVOKER (a SET clause or SECURITY DEFINER blocks inline_function; the SET-clause twin below shows the blocked form; whether STRICT would also block it is not tested), so the planner substitutes the body before it matches ORDER BY pathkeys against the index and the plan carries the operator, not this function's name. NexusTestCosineOrderInliningTest EXPLAINs it against a cosine_distance control; a plan that names nexus_test.cosine_order means the inlining failed.
changeSet.sql: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION nexus_test.cosine_order(a nexus.vector, b nexus.vector) RETURNS double precision LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE PARALLEL SAFE AS $$ SELECT a OPERATOR(nexus.<=>) b $$;
changeSet.rollback: DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS nexus_test.cosine_order(nexus.vector, nexus.vector)

changeSet.author: nexus-cbo4a
changeSet.comment: nexus_test.cosine_order_blocked(nexus.vector, nexus.vector): cosine_order's twin with one difference, a SET clause (pg_proc.proconfig is not null), which makes inline_function refuse it. It exists only as the detector's own control in NexusTestCosineOrderInliningTest: a plan that names this function, sorts and has no Order By line is what a failed inlining looks like, so the test proves its assertions can tell the two apart. Nothing else calls it.
changeSet.sql: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION nexus_test.cosine_order_blocked(a nexus.vector, b nexus.vector) RETURNS double precision LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE PARALLEL SAFE SET search_path = pg_catalog AS $$ SELECT a OPERATOR(nexus.<=>) b $$;
changeSet.rollback: DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS nexus_test.cosine_order_blocked(nexus.vector, nexus.vector)
